absent: Numeric compression-level table and window/hash/log parameters backing the compression block are not in these fragments.
Thread-pool lifecycle, job submission, and sequence-producer callback signature beyond the error sentinel are not shown.
Binary frame and block header layouts, checksum algorithm selection, and decoder state transitions beyond input-type names are not shown.
Errno-to-message mapping, fcntl command numbers, and open-flag interaction semantics beyond bit values are not shown.
Locking, concurrency, allocation failure handling, and stability guarantees beyond stable-buffer promises are not shown.

findings.text: Frame behaviour is governed by three integer toggles grouped together: whether a known content size appears in the header, whether a trailing checksum is emitted for error detection, and whether the dictionary identifier is omitted. Compression behaviour pairs a compression-parameter block with that frame-parameter block into one aggregate parameter object.

Dictionary intake distinguishes automatic detection of a dictionary magic header from forced raw-content treatment and forced full-dictionary validation that rejects inputs lacking the magic. Loading distinguishes copying bytes internally from referencing caller memory. Framing distinguishes the normal magic-prefixed frame from a magicless variant that saves four bytes but cannot be auto-recognised and needs explicit decoder selection.

Checksum handling is a binary validate-or-ignore switch, and decoder dictionary referencing is a single-versus-multiple switch. Dictionary attachment offers default heuristic, never-copy, always-copy and always-reload policies, with copy cost dominating tiny inputs and in-place use costing extra per-byte search. Literal handling offers automatic choice by level sign, forced Huffman attempt with uncompressed fallback, or forced uncompressed emission. Optional features share a tri-state automatic, forced-enable and forced-disable control.

Frame discovery yields a header record carrying content size with unknown and empty distinguished, window size bounded above by content size, maximum block size, a discriminator between normal and skippable frames, header size, dictionary identifier, checksum presence, and two reserved words. For skippable frames the size field reports skippable payload length and the identifier field reports the small magic variant.

Callers may inject allocation through a pair of opaque-context callbacks for allocate and release, bundled with the opaque pointer into a small record; a default all-null record defers to standard library allocation. Thread pooling is exposed only as an opaque incomplete structure type. Multithreaded progress is observed through counters for bytes ingested, consumed, produced and flushed plus current job identifier and active worker count, where flushed is caller-tracked.

Decoding input classification proceeds through frame header, block header, generic block, final block, checksum and skippable frame states. External sequence production can operate either without block delimiters or with explicit delimiters, and failures are signalled by an all-bits-set size value. Output margin planning accounts for worst-case frame header, trailing checksum, a small per-block overhead, and one full block of slack.

Stable compression parameter names are aliases of numbered experimental slots: rsyncable uses slot 1, format uses slot 2, force-max-window uses slot 3, force-attach-dict uses slot 4, literal-compression-mode uses slot 5, source-size-hint uses slot 7, dedicated-dict-search uses slot 8, stable input uses slot 9, stable output uses slot 10, block delimiters use slot 11, validate-sequences uses slot 12, split-after-sequences uses slot 13, row-match-finder uses slot 14, deterministic-ref-prefix uses slot 15, prefetch tables use slot 16, sequence-producer fallback uses slot 17, max block size uses slot 18, repcode resolution and its older external name share slot 19, and block-splitter level uses slot 20 with maximum level 6.

Stable decompression parameter names are aliases of numbered experimental slots: format uses slot 1, stable output uses slot 2, force-ignore-checksum uses slot 3, reference-multiple-dicts uses slot 4, disable Huffman assembly uses slot 5, and max block size uses slot 6.

The interface exposes narrow integer aliases for bytes, 16-bit units and long words, plus a checksum callback type that folds a buffer into a running check value. User register state for tracing is aliased to the native register structure. Allocation callbacks receive opaque context plus size or address, and the sequence-producer callback reports failure with the maximal size value.

An inline Adler helper computes a 32-bit checksum from two 16-bit halves with chunked accumulation and prime reduction, returns one when given no buffer, and otherwise processes input in bounded blocks with fast paths for multiples of sixteen and a scalar tail.

Deflate block kinds are numbered stored zero, static trees one and dynamic trees two. Match length is bounded between three and 258 inclusive. The preset-dictionary header bit is hex 20, the Unix OS code is 3, and Adler reduction uses prime 65521 with a maximum chunk of 5552 bytes before reduction.

Word width is either derived from character width times size of long or fixed at 32 depending on configuration, while long-long width is fixed at 64. Utility and UAPI headers use conventional include guards.

Generic base errors number 1 through 34 in ascending order from operation-not-permitted through math-range failure, covering lookup, process, I/O, descriptor, memory, permission, device, directory, argument, file-table, terminal, size, space, pipe and filesystem conditions. Selected values include try-again at 11, out-of-memory at 12, bad address at 14, invalid argument at 22, and broken pipe at 32.

Extended errors continue 35 through 134, adding deadlock, name length, locks, system call, directory, symlink, message, channel, link, device, stream, network, protocol, socket, address, connection, timeout, host, progress, staleness, quota, medium, cancellation, key and hardware conditions. The range starts with deadlock at 35 and ends with wrong file type at 134, with invalid system call at 38, already in progress at 114, required key missing at 126 and owner died at 130. Several names are aliases sharing one number: would-block shares try-again, deadlock long form shares its short form, bad CRC shares bad message, and filesystem-corrupted shares structure-needs-cleaning.

Access mode occupies the low two bits with a three-value mask: read-only zero, write-only bit zero, read-write bit one. Creation and behaviour flags use higher single bits: create at bit six, exclusive at bit seven, no-controlling-terminal at bit eight, truncate at bit nine, and append at bit ten, with several marked as not handled by the fcntl multiplexor.

Referencing dictionary memory requires the buffer to outlive every user, while magicless frames risk misdetection unless the decoder is explicitly configured. Requesting checksum suppression removes integrity detection, referencing multiple decoder dictionaries changes lifetime expectations, and promising stable input or output buffers forbids mutation or relocation during the call. The Adler helper treats a null buffer as a request for its initial value rather than an error.
